scenes.tts: In the first film, growth factors and amino acids switched em-tor C one on at the lysosome. But what stops a cell from building when its ATP starts running low? Running out of cellular ATP threatens survival fast. So a second master kinase, AMPK, serves as the cell's energy gauge.

scenes.visual: Same cell cross-section from the first film. On the right, emerald Rheb-GTP and gold mTORC1 glow active at the lysosome. On the left, an amber-orange fuel dial appears alongside a quiet three-part orange block labelled 'AMPK' (size 30). Ambient particle drift keeps the frame alive.
scenes.narration: In the first film, growth factors and amino acids switched mTORC1 on at the lysosome. But what stops a cell from building when its ATP starts running low? Running out of cellular ATP threatens survival fast. So a second master kinase, AMPK, serves as the cell's energy gauge.

scenes.tts: You might expect a fuel gauge to watch ATP itself. The catch is that a working cell holds ATP nearly steady, so ATP barely budges at first. Instead, the enzyme adenylate kinase balances two ADP against one ATP plus one AMP. So AMP tracks ADP squared, divided by ATP. When ATP dips just ten percent, AMP rises almost fourfold.

scenes.visual: Left half expands smoothly into a clean computed chart (labelled 'Computed: adenylate kinase, K = 0.5', size 26) plotting ATP, ADP, and AMP as ATP falls smoothly from rest (100%) to 80%: the emerald-white 'ATP' bar dips slightly, the yellow 'ADP' bar rises moderately, while the bright amber-red 'AMP' bar shoots dramatically upward (with '×1' climbing past '×4' to '×8' on screen; zero spoken numbers). A small amber low-fuel warning light flashes. Empathy fix: Numbers are now spoken: show '2 ADP ⇌ ATP + AMP' and 'AMP ∝ ADP² ÷ ATP' above the chart as they are said, then mark the 90% ATP point with the lesson's worked numbers 'ATP 5.0 → 4.5 mM, AMP 0.025 → 0.096 mM, ≈ ×4' as the ten percent dip is spoken (the AMP bar may continue to about ×8 at 80%).

scenes.tts: AMP works like a low-fuel warning light that trips while the needle has barely moved. AMPK has three subunits: alpha carries the kinase, and beta holds the complex together. The gamma subunit holds pockets where AMP and ATP compete, so it reads their ratio. Full activation needs a phosphate on alpha, added mainly by an always-active kinase called LKB one.

scenes.visual: Smoothly focus on the three-subunit orange AMPK complex (schematic blocks: 'Alpha (kinase)', 'Beta (scaffold)', 'Gamma (sensor)', size 28, no molecular structures). Glowing amber 'AMP' tokens stream from the spiking AMP bar into gamma, displacing dim ATP tokens. Above alpha, a steady block labelled 'LKB1' places a bright yellow 'P' onto alpha's activation loop (tagged 'Thr172' on screen). Empathy fix: Show 'Same pocket: AMP vs ATP' on the gamma subunit.

scenes.tts: If LKB one is always active, why does AMPK stay quiet in a rested cell? Because phosphatases keep stripping that phosphate back off. When AMP binds gamma, AMPK shifts shape so phosphatases cannot easily remove the phosphate. AMP also adds a direct allosteric boost, switching the kinase strongly on.

scenes.visual: Animation shows a grey 'Phosphatase' shape approaching alpha's 'P' tag and removing it when ATP occupies gamma. Then amber 'AMP' docks into gamma: the three subunits flex tightly inward, shielding the 'P' tag so the phosphatase bounces off harmlessly. The alpha kinase flares bright orange-red ('AMPK ON', size 30).

scenes.tts: Now put both gauges in one cell. Growth factors and amino acids are plentiful, but ATP dips and AMPK switches on, and it vetoes growth. One veto route runs through the TSC brake. So test it. Suppose a cell has lost TSC two, a key part of that brake. Can AMPK still shut the growth kinase down?

scenes.visual: Pull back to the full cell cross-section combining both halves: on the right, emerald growth factor and cyan amino acids remain present with gold mTORC1 glowing on the lysosome; on the left, bright orange-red 'AMPK ON' pulses. The crimson 'TSC2' block on the lysosome rim fades to a dashed grey outline with a small 'missing' tag, and emerald Rheb stays lit. Top question banner (size 30): 'No TSC2, ATP falling: can AMPK still turn mTORC1 down?' Empathy fix: Add a small tag 'TSC2 = subunit of TSC'.

scenes.visual: Hold the predict frame with ambient motion: emerald and cyan signals pulse on the right, the dashed grey 'TSC2 missing' outline stays on the lysosome rim, and bright orange-red AMPK pulses on the left; a quiet circular progress ring fills in the top-right corner over 4.5 seconds while the question banner stays on screen.

scenes.tts: Partly, yes, because AMPK carries two separate brakes. Normally it phosphorylates TSC two at activating sites, turning the TSC brake back on and draining Rheb of GTP. But AMPK also phosphorylates Raptor, a part of em-tor C one itself, braking the complex directly. So even without TSC two, energy stress can still dim protein building.

scenes.visual: Question banner fades. A small inset labelled 'Normal cell' (size 26) shows active AMPK stamping a 'P' onto crimson 'TSC2', which clamps Rheb so Rheb flips to dim grey 'GDP'. In the main frame, where TSC2 is a dashed grey outline and Rheb stays emerald, AMPK fires one bright amber arc that stamps a 'P' onto gold 'Raptor'. Gold mTORC1 dims partway ('mTORC1 dimmed', size 30), and the protein-synthesis arrow thins but does not vanish. Empathy fix: Label 'Raptor (mTORC1 subunit)'.

scenes.tts: At the same time, AMPK rebalances the cell's energy budget. It cuts spending by switching off enzymes that build fat and cholesterol. The first fat-building enzyme also makes a blocker of fatty acid entry into mitochondria. Switching it off opens that door, so fat is burned for fuel. In muscle, AMPK brings more glucose transporters to the surface to raise fuel income.

scenes.tts: So AMPK reads rising AMP to conserve energy and veto em-tor C one. Gamma senses AMP against ATP, while ADP and calcium signals can also tune this switch. That energy veto overrides both growth yeses whenever fuel runs short. Protecting cellular energy comes before building new protein.
